description: A powerful cross-platform port management tool for developers. Monitor ports, manage Kubernetes port forwards, integrate Cloudflare Tunnels, and kill processes with one click.

sources.entry: PortKiller - Tool for inspecting ports, managing forwards and tunnels, and stopping bound processes. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/productdevbook/port-killer)

summary.one_liner: PortKiller is a menu bar app for macOS and a system tray app for Windows that lists listening TCP ports, kills processes bound to them, and manages Kubernetes port-forward sessions and Cloudflare Tunnel connections.
summary.what_it_does: PortKiller auto-discovers all listening TCP ports and shows the process behind each one, with search and filtering by port number or process name. It can terminate a process with one click, using graceful stop or force kill. Ports can be marked as favorites or watched for notifications, and are grouped into categories such as Web Server, Database, Development, and System. It can create and manage kubectl port-forward sessions, with auto-reconnect, connection logs, and connect/disconnect notifications. It also shows active Cloudflare Tunnel connections with quick access to tunnel status. The README describes a macOS menu bar app and a Windows system tray app.
use_cases: find which process is using a port
watch specific ports and get notified
how_to_run: Or download the .dmg from GitHub Releases (macOS)
Or download the .zip from GitHub Releases and extract (Windows)
notable: Cross-platform: macOS menu bar app and Windows system tray app
Combines port killing with kubectl port-forward management and Cloudflare Tunnel status in one tool
Graceful and force kill options for terminating processes
caveats: README gives little detail on Windows features; the Windows section only says to download and extract the zip
Kubernetes port forwarding depends on kubectl being available, and Cloudflare Tunnel support is limited to viewing and managing active connections
README does not state platform minimum versions or detailed system requirements
